summary: The study describes the atomic layer deposition of GdCoO3 and Gd0.9Ca0.1CoO3 using β-diketonates and ozone as precursors. The films are amorphous as deposited and become crystalline after post-annealing at 650 °C. The process allows for the tuning of crystal orientation and is suitable for high-surface-area substrates, with potential applications in catalysis.
evidence: Thin ﬁlms of the catalytically interesting ternary and quaternary perovskites GdCoO3 and Gd0.9Ca0.1CoO3 are fabricated by atomic layer deposition using metal β-diketonates and ozone as precursors. The resulting thin ﬁlms are amorphous as deposited and become single-oriented crystalline on LaAlO3(100) and YAlO3(100/010) after post-annealing at 650◦C in air. The crystal orientations of the ﬁlms are tunable by choice and the orientation of the substrate, mitigated through the interface via solid face epitaxy upon annealing. We believe that coatings of GdCoO3 and Gd1−xCaxCoO3 may ﬁnd applications within oxidation catalysis.
